title: Ridgecrest Insurance — inference onboarding diary
body:
Context / meeting: 2025-10-28 11:00 PT with Ridgecrest infra + data teams (Alice Tan - infra, Ben Russo - app lead, Clara Vigo - security). Quick sync after initial discovery call. Goal: capture requirements, gotchas, next steps for a small PoC of private inference (VPC) + optional Dedicated capacity for peak periods. Notes are messy — capture raw.

Attendees (Redwood): Samira Khan (SE, owner), Marcus Lee (SRE support), Priya Desai (security consultant - async)

Agenda we ran through (rough):
- High-level: latency / cost SLOs, data residency / PHI concerns
- Integration options: Private (customer-managed VPC) vs Dedicated (reserved) vs hybrid
- Model choice: open LLM candidate suggestions and quantization tradeoffs
- Timeline / PoC scope and success metrics

Key customer constraints / asks:
- Data residency: all inference requests must stay in customer AWS account in us-east-2. No payloads to external APIs. (sensitive underwriting data incl. SSN-like tokens occasionally)
- Compliance: Ridgecrest uses a third-party KMS (GemSafe) and HSM-backed key storage for any model artifacts and audit logs. Need KMS integration notes.
- Throughput target: steady-state ~300 requests/minute, spikes to ~900 req/min during batch underwriting windows (02:00–03:00 daily). Typical prompt size: 200–600 tokens; averages ~340 input tokens, 150 generated tokens.
- Latency goal: p95 < 350ms for inference on primary flows; can accept degraded p95 up to 700ms for non-critical batch scoring.
- Model accuracy: low tolerance for hallucinations on policy clauses; want deterministic-ish outputs where feasible (score + extractive answers)
- Cost sensitivity: they want an estimated cost per 1M requests and guidance on quantization that doesn’t break accuracy for legal text extraction.

Integration gotchas & red flags (from their infra):
- VPN / transit: Ridgecrest has a legacy IPSEC concentrator and restrictive outbound NAT — our private control plane cannot reach their VPC without a dedicated peering arrangement. Need SRE to confirm options: AWS Transit Gateway vs site-to-site. Marcus to follow up with network patterns.
- GemSafe KMS: not a standard AWS KMS. We need HSM signing integration or a bring-your-own-key adapter; product currently supports AWS KMS and external HSM via KMIP — confirm GemSafe compatibility. Priya to own a short compatibility matrix.
- Large context windows cause OOM in quantized kernels for some open models. They indicated some prompts include full policy text (~4–6k tokens) plus claimant history (~3k) — total > 8k in worst cases. Our suggestion: prefix caching + summary pipeline; also discuss model stitching (extract then generate) to reduce max_seq_len.
- Observability requirements: Ridgecrest wants per-request audit trail stored for 2y and token-level cost attribution. Storage must be in their account (S3) and encrypted with GemSafe. We need an integration path for logs delivery and retention.
- Legal wants an SLA clause for data deletion on contract termination (30 days). Need confirmation that private deployments can purge logs and model cache per-seat.

Model choices discussed (notes):
- Candidate family: open models fine (LlamaX-like), but they prefer variants with strong instruction-following and legal-domain fine-tuning. Discussed using a smaller encoder+extractor followed by a generator for final text to control hallucination.
- Quantization: 4-bit + group-quant seemed attractive for cost. Need to run regression tests on claim-extraction prompt set.

Preliminary PoC scope (customer agreed to):
- Deploy private control plane + one inference pool in their us-east-2 account (single AZ) behind a dedicated subnet with peered routing.
- Model: 1 candidate open model (to be selected) quantized to the recommended profile; fallback to unquantized if regressions are >3% accuracy delta on baseline eval set.
- Workload: a 2-week trial with synthetic replay of 1M requests/day at representative distributions (steady + spike window). We'll run initial perf tests at 50%, 75%, 100% of target throughput.
- Observability: deliver audit stream to S3 + CloudWatch metrics to their account; token-level cost drilldown daily.

Success metrics for PoC (agreed):
- p95 latency <= 350ms at 70% of steady throughput; acceptable degradation to 700ms during spikes.
- Extraction accuracy delta <= 3% vs current human baseline on the 120-case eval set (we need to collect cases)
- No data egress outside their account; logs encrypted with GemSafe or equivalent

Action items / owners (raw):
- Samira: write PoC plan + architecture diagram + initial runbook by 2025-11-06 (deliver to Alice + Ben)
- Marcus: network options doc (Transit Gateway vs site-to-site vs VPC peering) + estimated effort by 2025-11-07
- Priya: KMS/HSM compatibility checklist & legal requirements (GemSafe specifics) by 2025-11-05
- Ben (Ridgecrest): provide sample payloads (anonymized) and 120-case eval set by 2025-11-08
- Clara (Ridgecrest security): confirm retention policy and deletion process; expect questions on audit trail schema — scheduled follow-up 2025-11-04
- Infra: quick perf sanity run (local sim) using 2 x A10G-equivalent nodes; aim to have numbers by 2025-11-10 (Marcus + infra)

Open / unresolved questions (we should push on):
- GemSafe integration path: can we store model artifacts' encryption keys with GemSafe or must we manage separate key wrapping? Is KMIP endpoint available?
- Peak concurrency pattern: need exact percentile distribution for the 02:00–03:00 spike (are spikes short bursts or sustained 1hr ramp?). This affects autoscaler config.
- Long-context cases: do we need to support >12k tokens? If so, hybrid approach required (summarize + external KV store). Get samples.
- Legal: specific language about data deletion and forensic access. Ask legal to draft an SLA stub.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: GemSafe incompatibility delays PoC. Mitigation: propose sidecar KMS adapter or vault-based wrap in short-term.
- Risk: OOMs on quantized kernels with worst-case length. Mitigation: progressive rollout (quantized -> mixed -> full fp16) and run regression suite early.
- Risk: Network peering complexity. Mitigation: propose two paths and run a small connectivity pilot first.

Meeting follow-up plan (quick):
1) Email Ridgecrest with PoC outline + requested artifacts list (Samira, today 2025-10-28)
2) Setup technical deep-dive (Marcus + Priya) with their infra team — target 2025-11-03
3) Internal triage: prioritize KMS compatibility and network path in next sprint (infra + security)

Notes-to-self / informal:
- Keep PoC lean: prefer one model + solid instrumentation rather than multi-model matrix up front.
- Need to build a short eval harness for legal/extractive prompts — include human in loop for initial 120 cases.
- Pricing: prepare two asks — minimal PoC estimate (SaaS + infra) and scaled Dedicated commit estimate (monthly). UX wants clear callouts about unit cost drivers: tokens, context length, batching.

Next sync: 2025-11-04 follow-up to confirm Clara's retention answer and for Ridgecrest to share eval set.
